title: Asphalt Fumes During Roofing Operations
summary: Asphalt kettle fumes cause headaches, nausea, and drowsiness and are linked to lung cancer. Hotter asphalt makes more fumes. This talk covers kettle placement, temperature control, and PPE.
talking_points: Place the kettle downwind on firm, level ground where the operator and others get the least fume exposure. Keep plenty of cross-breeze.
Never set the kettle in a confined space where fumes can build up. Keep the lid closed as much as possible and fill through the loading door, not the lid.
Keep the asphalt at the lowest temperature needed. Do not turn it up for a faster melt. Stay at least 25 degrees below the asphalt's flash point.
Pre-chop asphalt into small, easy-to-melt pieces before loading.
Wear a hard hat, face shield, goggles, long sleeves, gloves, and leather boots.
Have the supervisor rope off the area around the kettle with tape, cones, or signs. Keep a fully charged ABC fire extinguisher nearby and clear fire hazards from the area.
site_hazards_to_check: Kettle placed upwind, in a low spot, or in an enclosed area where fumes collect
Damaged or leaking kettle lid, or broken temperature controls
Kettle temperature within 25 degrees of the asphalt flash point
Fire hazards near the kettle and missing or discharged ABC extinguisher
Unmarked area around the kettle with no cones, tape, or signs
discussion_questions: Which way is the wind blowing today, and where should the kettle go?
What is the flash point of the asphalt we are using, and what temperature will we hold?
What symptoms tell you that you have had too much fume exposure, and what do you do then?

Content - place the kettle downwind on firm level ground with good cross-breeze, never in a confined space, keep the lid closed and load through the door, hold the lowest workable temperature and stay at least 25 F below the flash point, pre-chop asphalt, wear hard hat/face shield/goggles/long sleeves/gloves/leather boots, rope off the kettle area, keep a charged ABC extinguisher and clear fire hazards - is consistent with NIOSH asphalt-roofing recommendations.
